question: Graviera Kritis PDO cheese is one of the most emblematic Cretan agri-food products. It has a direct link with sheep and goat farming, the economic viability of mountainous areas and the preservation of Crete’s food-producing tradition and cultural identity.

The establishment of an inter-branch organisation involving producers and manufacturers opens up significant prospects for better coordination of the chain, stronger protection of the designation, more effective marketing of the product and support for livestock farmers.

Strengthening the bargaining position of producers through producer organisations, associations and inter-branch organisations is a key priority of the common agricultural policy (CAP). The creation of the inter-branch organisation for Graviera Kritis PDO is an opportunity to strengthen the collective organisation of the sector, in view also of the new CAP.
In light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What possibilities for financial and technical support can be leveraged for the introduction, recognition and operation of the inter-branch organisation for Graviera Kritis PDO, for designation protection and marketing actions?
Does it intend, in the context of the new CAP, to strengthen incentives and funding for producer organisations and inter-branch organisations, particularly in countries with a less structured setup?

What European collective organisation practices in the dairy and cheese sector could be leveraged to strengthen the position of Cretan livestock farmers and give the Graviera Kritis PDO even more visibility on the markets?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.10.2026) Greece may decide to grant EU support for setting-up an interbranch organisation1 recognised for ‘Graviera Kritis’ cheese with a protected designation of origin (PDO).

Support is limited to 10 % of the value of the annual marketed production of the organisation, with a maximum of EUR 100 000 per year; support is degressive and limited to the first five years following recognition. This type of support is proposed to be reconducted under the next CAP for the period 2028-20342.

Producers of ‘Graviera Kritis’ PDO cheese could also decide to set-up a recognised producer organisation (PO) benefiting from the setting-up EU support as described above, with a view to planning production, concentrating supply and putting on the market their production through the PO.

Should Greece decide to include support for setting-up POs in its National Strategic Plan, the PO could subsequently start implementing an operational programme benefiting from EU financial support3 to strengthen its long-term competitiveness4, in particular by implementing actions related to the PDO and marketing.
Producer organisations and interbranch organisations are important tools for reinforcing the position of farmers in the food supply chain.

Producer groups as referred to in Article 32 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1143 can also play a key role to improve the performance of the geographical indication, for instance by entering into private supply management arrangements pursuant to Article 166a of Regulation (EU) No 1308/20135.
1 Article 77(8), point (b), of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115. 2 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing the conditions for the

implementation of the Union support to the Common Agriculture, Policy for the period from 2028-2034 (COM/2025/560). 3 Articles 66 to 67 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 4 https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/common-agricultural-policy/agri-food-supply-chain/producer-and-interbranchorganisations_en#producerorganisations.

5 Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 December 2013 establishing a common organisation of the markets in agricultural products and repealing Council Regulations (EEC) No 922/72, (EEC) No 234/79, (EC) No 1037/2001 and (EC) No 1234/2007.
